stem: The graph of the linear function \(g\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. For which values of \(x\) is \(g(x) > 2\)?
solution: The line passes through \((0, -4)\) and \((2, 0)\), so its slope is \(\frac{0 - (-4)}{2 - 0} = 2\) and \(g(x) = 2x - 4\).
On the graph, the line is above \(y = 2\) to the right of \(x = 3\).

explanation.A: Incorrect. This stops at \(2x > 6\) without dividing by 2.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The line rises from left to right, so \(g(x)\) is greater than 2 to the right of \(x = 3\), not to the left.
explanation.D: Incorrect. \(x = 2\) is where \(g(x) = 0\), the \(x\)-intercept, not where \(g(x) = 2\).

verify:
P = lambda s: value(s.replace('\\le', '<=').replace('\\ge', '>='))
x = symbols('x')
g = sympify(figure['curves'][0]['expr'])
s = solve_univariate_inequality(g > 2, x, relational=False)
assert s == Interval.open(3, oo)
assert solve_univariate_inequality(P(choices[answer]), x, relational=False) == s
assert all(solve_univariate_inequality(P(choices[k]), x, relational=False) != s for k in choices if k != answer)
